newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Air says revs firm despite load factors.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Air says revs firm despite load factors.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Co has seen its load factors drop in the first half of 1997 but revenues remain strong, Chief Financial Officer Gary Kelly said.

"We have seen somewhat softer load factors in '97 but we have been very pleased with the overall revenues production that we've seen," Kelly told reporters in a meeting at the carrier's Dallas headquarters.
He said the airline's ticket prices have been firm because it has gone easy on promotional campaigns.
Kelly declined to provide details of revenues per available seat mile in the second quarter but said they remain strong despite the reintroduction of a 10 percent federal excise tax in March.

He said costs had been helped by a sharp reduction in jet fuel prices to about 57-58 cents per gallon currently, and by Southwest's own cost-reduction initiatives. "They are consuming a great deal of effort and fortunately they are paying off big," he said.
